quantum_risk.rationale: Public-key primitives (RSA, ECC) are vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on a future cryptographically-relevant quantum computer (CRQC). Ciphertext captured today can be decrypted later (Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later), and long-lived signatures forged - which is why PQC migration is time-critical.

waves.name: Wave 1 — Classical-weak remediation & HNDL triage
waves.criteria: Classical-weak security-use crypto (MD5, SHA-1, DES, 3DES, RC4, RC2, Blowfish), HNDL-exposed or internet-facing key establishment, inventory gaps.
waves.focus: Remediate classically broken/deprecated primitives, rotate HNDL-exposed keys, add hybrid handshakes, and stage urgent PQC replacements for publicly exposed assets.

waves.name: Wave 2 — Post-quantum migration
waves.criteria: Remaining Shor-vulnerable public-key primitives (RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, DH, Ed25519), hybrid KEM deployment, PQC signature migration, certificate chain rotation.
waves.focus: Systematically move public-key signatures and key exchange to ML-KEM / ML-DSA per CNSA 2.0, covering downstream trust chains.

waves.name: Wave 3 — Symmetric hardening & governance
waves.criteria: Symmetric cipher consolidation (AES-256-GCM), hash strengthening, governance codification, crypto policy guardrails in CI.
waves.focus: Consolidate symmetric modes (AES-256-GCM), strengthen hashes to SHA-256+/SHA-3, retire legacy ciphers, and codify crypto policy so new failures cannot ship.

recommendations.description: 0 canonical asset(s) face harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure. Rotate affected keys/certificates and introduce hybrid TLS handshakes before any large-scale PQC migration.

recommendations.description: 5 canonical asset(s) use Shor-vulnerable public-key primitives on a internal surface. Migrate to NIST PQC (ML-KEM/ML-DSA) with hybrid transition where interoperability requires.

recommendations.description: Consolidate data-at-rest to AES-256-GCM and strengthen hashes to SHA-256/SHA-3; retire legacy cipher references.

executive_summary: The ECDAT Enterprise Post-Quantum Cryptographic Risk Report evaluated 10 cryptographic assets across the internal application environment, identifying 6 high-risk and 5 quantum-vulnerable items concentrated entirely within the 'unknown' service. Although no urgent or critical risk priorities currently exist, the complete inventory requires structured mitigation across designated multi-quarter waves. Strategic remediation focuses on modernizing vulnerable assets and embedding post-quantum cryptographic standards to safeguard internal operations against future quantum threats.
quantum_risk_narrative: Public-key primitives like RSA and ECC are fundamentally vulnerable to Shor's algorithm executed on future cryptographically-relevant quantum computers. Because ciphertext intercepted today can be decrypted retroactively and long-lived signatures forged, migrating to quantum-resilient algorithms is an urgent operational priority.

strategic_recommendations.title: Wave 1 Triage and Assessment
strategic_recommendations.description: Perform comprehensive asset discovery and standards triage on the 'unknown' service to catalog all legacy and unclassified cryptographic usages.

strategic_recommendations.title: Wave 2 Post-Quantum Migration
strategic_recommendations.description: Execute phased replacement of all quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms and deprecated symmetric primitives with approved NIST PQC standards.

strategic_recommendations.title: Wave 3 Symmetric Hardening & Governance
strategic_recommendations.description: Establish continuous cryptographic governance, enforce robust key rotation schedules, and ensure long-term symmetric resilience.
